title: Isabell Springer, PhD (Founder/CEO, SHiFT) — 'Are incorruptible leaders born, or can we develop them?'
summary: Isabell Springer, PhD, LMFT — founder and CEO of SHiFT and a two-decade trauma therapist — publishes a long LinkedIn reflection on Incorruptible, arguing that governance and structure aren't enough. Every mission-protecting system is ultimately operated by a human being who has to hold under pressure. She sketches SHiFT's Catch-Call-Choose-Own-Return pathway as the emotional-capacity layer that makes structural incorruptibility actually work.
blockquote:
I've been reading Eric Ries Incorruptible, and I keep coming back to a question underneath the ideas in the book.

Are incorruptible leaders born, or can we develop them? Nature versus nurture. Corruptible versus incorruptible.

We can build governance structures that protect a company's mission. We can choose the right investors, define fiduciary responsibilities, and embed purpose into the organization. But eventually, a human being has to make a decision.

What happens when protecting the mission costs you something?
